about: Who speaks and how they sound. Voices are DESIGNED from a text description by Breeze-TTS-2 (Trap Door's pipeline, copied: tools/tts there is read-only to us); no real person is named, imitated or cloned. 'fx' picks the radio treatment in tools/audio (Radio.cs): crew = band-limited, a little saturation, squelch in and out; earth = vast, cold, reverberant, machine-edged; alien = a layered, inhuman vocal texture. Speaker names are matched case-insensitively against the radio line's callsign (the part before the colon) and against #Name for voices off the battlefield. Intensity (user, 2026-10-24: battles must sound frantic, not calm): every line is tagged calm, tense or frantic from its mission context (see collect_lines.py); a tense or frantic line is generated with the voice's instruction plus the modifier below, a punctuated version of its text, and then sped, pitched up, squeezed of pauses, breathed and distorted (Dsp/Radio.cs). Earth never panics. No Scottish accents; accents in use: South African, Irish, Australian, London, Texan, Northern English, alien.

mercy.who: The Small Mercy's comms officer (diaspora cruiser)
mercy.instruction: A calm, dry, middle-aged woman with a South African English accent, speaking as a warship's communications officer over a ship-to-ship radio. Low, steady and understated, deadpan, with the weary gallows humour of someone who has seen too much. Clear diction, an even pace.
mercy.identity: A middle-aged woman with a South African English accent and a low voice, a warship's communications officer speaking over a ship-to-ship radio. Clear diction.

tamsin.instruction: An older Irish woman with a hoarse, tired voice, the captain of a crippled freighter, speaking tersely over a bad radio. Dry and deadpan, exasperated but in control, slightly breathless, never panicking, never shouting.
tamsin.identity: An older Irish woman with a hoarse, rough voice, the captain of a crippled freighter, speaking over a bad radio.

sable2.instruction: A young Australian man with a low, relaxed, slightly husky baritone voice, a starfighter pilot speaking quietly and calmly over the radio. Laconic, dry, deadpan and unhurried, understated, with a hint of black humour. Low-pitched and a little tired.
sable2.identity: A young Australian man with a low, slightly husky baritone voice, a starfighter pilot speaking over the radio.

sable3.instruction: A young woman with a London accent, a starfighter pilot speaking over the radio, quick, wry and dry. Clipped and calm under pressure, deadpan delivery, understated sarcasm, a little husky.
sable3.identity: A young woman with a London accent and a slightly husky voice, a starfighter pilot speaking over the radio.

sable1.who: Sable 1, the player's own voice when a line falls to them (no wingman left to say it)
sable1.instruction: A man in his thirties with a calm, level, slightly weary voice and a Northern English accent from Manchester, a starfighter pilot speaking quietly over the radio. Dry, deadpan and understated, with a hint of black humour; low and steady.
sable1.identity: A man in his thirties with a Northern English accent from Manchester, a starfighter pilot speaking over the radio.

lantern.instruction: A very deep, low-pitched, gravelly middle-aged American man with a slow Texas drawl, a starfighter squadron leader on the radio. Easygoing, unhurried and dry, with deadpan wry humour, calm, rough and rumbling like gravel.
lantern.identity: A very deep, low-pitched, gravelly middle-aged American man with a Texas drawl, a starfighter squadron leader on the radio.

wick.instruction: A non-human alien speaking English: a deep, resonant, breathy voice with a strange, layered, whistling and clicking timbre, unhuman cadence and unusual vowels. Slow, deliberate and calm, with a quiet dry amusement. Speaking over a radio.
wick.identity: A non-human alien speaking English: a deep, resonant, breathy voice with a strange, layered, whistling and clicking timbre, unhuman cadence and unusual vowels. Speaking over a radio.

delivery.tense: Agitated and quicker than usual: the layered, whistling timbre sharpening, an unhuman urgency.
delivery.frantic: Shrill and agitated, the layered whistling voice cracking and overlapping, fast, an unhuman alarm.

earth_warden.who: Earth, through its corvette the Warden (and any unnamed Earth voice)
earth_warden.instruction: A vast, cold, genderless voice of immense authority, reading scripture aloud. Very deep and resonant, perfectly enunciated, slow and measured, completely without emotion or warmth, contemptuous and serene, like a machine that believes it is a god.

earth_lector.who: Earth, through its picket corvette the Lector
earth_lector.instruction: An ancient, hollow, whispering and precise voice, very deep and slow, a priest-machine delivering a sentence. Cold, calm, without any emotion, every syllable perfectly formed and deliberate, faintly metallic, vast and unhurried.

intensity.about: Delivery appended to a voice's 'identity' for a tense or frantic line (a calm line uses the voice's full 'instruction'). Per-voice 'delivery' overrides it.
intensity.tense: Under fire and speaking fast and urgently: tight, clipped and slightly breathless, strain in the voice, louder than normal, still dry underneath, with a flash of grim humour.
intensity.frantic: Panicked and shouting over the roar of battle, adrenaline pounding: very fast, loud, breathless and clipped, the voice straining and cracking, desperate urgency, gasping between phrases, yelling, yet still with a bitter flash of gallows humour, like a marine in a firefight.
